description: Bounded VCO: an oscillator whose triangle climbs to a ceiling voltage, turns and falls to a floor voltage, with separate control of the two slopes, after Peter Blasser's Bound/Bounce circuits

params.text: Switches the FREQ knob between audio rates of about 8Hz to 8372Hz, 261.63Hz at noon, and low frequency rates of 0.0625Hz to 64Hz, 2Hz at noon
Cycles the oversampling applied against aliasing: off, then x2, x4, x8, x16 and x32
Turned on, the floor and the ceiling are exchanged whenever the floor is the higher of the two; turned off the triangle follows the floor upward instead
Sets the rate of the triangle, marked for a 10V gap between floor and ceiling; a narrower gap raises the rate and a wider one lowers it
Sets the share of the cycle spent rising, 1% for a falling ramp, 50% for a symmetrical triangle and 99% for a rising ramp
Attenuates and inverts the FREQ CV input, and at 100% that input is scaled a volt per octave
Attenuates and inverts the SKEW CV input, and at 100% each volt moves the rising share by 10%
Sets the voltage the triangle falls to, -10V to 10V and starting at -5V, summed with the FLOOR CV input and clamped between -12V and 12V
Sets the voltage the triangle climbs to, -10V to 10V and starting at 5V, summed with the CEILING CV input and clamped between -12V and 12V
Attenuates and inverts the FLOOR CV input
Attenuates and inverts the CEILING CV input

inputs.text: Raises and lowers the rate, added to the FREQ knob through the attenuverter beneath that knob, and it can drive the rate past the knob's own range
Moves the rising share of the cycle, added to the SKEW knob through the attenuverter beneath that knob; the total is held between 1% and 99%
Moves the floor voltage, added to the FLOOR knob through the attenuverter beneath that knob
Moves the ceiling voltage, added to the CEILING knob through the attenuverter beneath that knob

outputs.text: Carries 5V while the triangle is rising and -5V while it is falling
The triangle itself, running between the floor and the ceiling, so its amplitude is the gap between them and it can be unipolar or bipolar; brief excursions past a bound do occur

notes: every input takes polyphony, and the outputs carry as many channels as the widest input; a monophonic input is copied to every channel
a polyphonic input with too few channels reads 0V for the channels it lacks
all four CV inputs can be driven at audio rates

inputs.1:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±12V.
inputs.3:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±12V.
